basics.name: Yitong Bai
basics.label: M.S. Student in Computer Engineering, Columbia University
basics.summary: Research interests: LLM agents, multi-agent systems, ML systems, evaluation and verification, reproducibility, trustworthy AI, and LLM post-training.

work.name: National Zhijiang Lab
work.summary: Advisor: Jiaxi Yang, Research Scientist, National Zhijiang Lab. Project: Feedback Learning for EHR SQL Repair: SFT vs. GRPO; manuscript in preparation.
highlights: Conducted a pre-registered study comparing SFT and GRPO on how diagnostic feedback shapes learning for EHR SQL repair.
Fine-tuned Qwen3.5-9B on MIMIC-IV EHR questions under four nested feedback levels, from a bare failure signal to repair hints.
Trained 12 QLoRA adapters across four feedback conditions and three seeds, and evaluated 13 model groups across 10,400 repair records.
Built a target-free GRPO pipeline with a binary execution reward and observed an exploratory L2 feedback signal of +10.0 points, pending multi-seed confirmation.

work.name: Columbia University, CRIS Lab
work.summary: Advisor: Prof. Venkat Venkatasubramanian. Project: DeepAudit: Agentic Evidence-Based Auditing of ML Reproducibility; manuscript in preparation.
highlights: Designed and implemented DeepAudit, an agentic claim-level reproducibility auditing system for ML papers and companion repositories.

Built a 23-step Python pipeline covering PDF-to-Markdown ingestion, table/figure-aware claim extraction, repository analysis, RAG-assisted code indexing, environment repair, autonomous execution, evidence alignment, scoring, and report generation.
Evaluated DeepAudit on 10 public ML paper-code pairs with 64 pre-specified audit targets, extracting 1,101 claims and executing 52/64 experiment specifications.

work.name: Columbia University / IBM Research Collaboration
work.summary: Mentored by Dhaval Patel, Senior Technical Staff Member, IBM Research. Project: Multi-Turn AssetOps: Supervisor-Specialist Agents for Industrial O&M.
highlights: Proposed and designed a LangGraph-based Supervisor-Specialist multi-agent architecture for multi-turn industrial asset operations and maintenance.
Designed structured cross-turn artifact reuse for sensor evidence, anomaly analyses, failure hypotheses, and maintenance recommendations.
Optimized routing, artifact reuse, and MCP execution with constraints, schema validation, duplicate-call suppression, and failure guards.
Co-developed and evaluated 16 multi-turn industrial dialogs, reporting gains in planning effectiveness, task completion, tool-time share, and follow-up latency after artifact reuse.

work.name: SJTU Summer Campus
highlights: Built a facial emotion recognition pipeline on the FER-2013 dataset using VGG16-based feature extraction and an MLP classifier.
Led a four-person team and completed the implementation and project report.

work.name: Neusoft Group
highlights: Contributed to development and testing for a university portal system, including frontend refinement, database interface support, and cross-database data matching.
Worked with heterogeneous data sources to support synchronization and integration across subsystems.
